description: Dashboard voice button (PRIMARY). Add speech INPUT to the Overview/voice console: a mic toggle button next to Send plus a BCP-47 language <select>, both built with el() from dom.js. Clicking the mic starts browser SpeechRecognition in the selected language, puts interim transcript live into the existing input, and on final result calls the existing send() (which already POSTs /api/assist and speaks the reply via speakPreview). Also extend speakPreview so the reply is spoken in the selected language. Frontend-only (voice.js + agents.js); independent of FEAT-002.
steps: Read .agents/tasks/task-voice-nl/context.json and this file FIRST. Then read jarvis-backend/src/jarvis_backend/web/js/views/voice.js, jarvis-backend/src/jarvis_backend/web/js/views/agents.js, and jarvis-backend/src/jarvis_backend/web/js/dom.js to confirm the el()/send()/setState()/speakPreview() shapes described in context.json.

In voice.js (mountOverview), add a small editable language list near the top of the module: const LANGS = [['en-US','English'],['hi-IN','Hindi'],['es-ES','Spanish'],['fr-FR','French'],['de-DE','German'],['ar-SA','Arabic'],['zh-CN','Chinese']]; and a module/closure variable let sessionLang = (localStorage.getItem('jarvis.voiceLang') || document.documentElement.lang || 'en-US'); keep logic reading sessionLang (do NOT hardcode the 7 codes anywhere except this array).

Build the language <select> with el('select', {...}) + LANGS.map(([code,label]) => el('option', { value: code, selected: code===sessionLang }, label)); on change set sessionLang = e.target.value and persist localStorage.setItem('jarvis.voiceLang', sessionLang). Give it an aria-label like 'Voice language'.

Build a mic toggle button with el('button', { class:'btn', type:'button', 'aria-label':'Start voice input', 'aria-pressed':'false', onClick: toggleMic }, 'Mic') placed in the same row as the existing Send button.

Add const SR = window.SpeechRecognition || window.webkitSpeechRecognition; If SR is undefined, set the mic button disabled=true and, on an attempted click, toast('Voice input needs Chrome or Edge','') — never throw. Keep a module-scoped `let recognition = null; let listening = false;`.

Implement toggleMic(): if listening, call recognition.stop() and return (toggle semantics). Otherwise: window.speechSynthesis.cancel() for barge-in; create recognition = new SR(); set recognition.continuous=false, recognition.interimResults=true, recognition.lang = sessionLang; set listening=true, update button aria-pressed='true', and setState('LISTENING','Speak now','listening').

Wire recognition handlers: onresult builds a transcript from event.results; write interim text live into the existing `input` (input.value = interim); when a result isFinal, set input.value to the final text; onend sets listening=false, aria-pressed='false', resets the button, and if the input has final text calls send() (send() already clears input, posts /api/assist, and speaks the reply); onerror (e.g. 'not-allowed' denied mic, 'no-speech' timeout) toasts a short message and cleanly resets to READY via setState('READY','Say “Hey JARVIS”','') without throwing.
In the send() reply path, change the existing speakPreview(r.speech, v) call to speakPreview(r.speech, v, sessionLang) so the reply is spoken in the selected language.

In agents.js, extend speakPreview(text, voice, langOverride) with langOverride optional and defaulted: utterance.lang = langOverride || voice.language || 'en-US'; after creating the utterance, select a matching system voice: const match = (window.speechSynthesis.getVoices()||[]).find(v => v.lang && v.lang.toLowerCase().startsWith(utterance.lang.slice(0,2).toLowerCase())); if (match) utterance.voice = match; — leave default voice when none matches. Do NOT change the pitch/rate clamping. Confirm the other existing caller in agents.js (speakPreview(text, agent.voice)) still works because the new param is optional.
Review the diff: ensure ONLY el()/textContent are used (NO innerHTML), nothing inline is injected, no CDN/third-party import, and the SR-absent branch disables the button gracefully.
acceptance_criteria: voice.js adds a mic toggle button and a BCP-47 language <select>, both built via el() from dom.js, with no innerHTML and no inline script/style.
When window.SpeechRecognition/webkitSpeechRecognition is undefined, the mic button is disabled and a click path toasts 'Voice input needs Chrome or Edge' without throwing.

Starting recognition cancels speechSynthesis (barge-in), sets continuous=false/interimResults=true/lang=sessionLang, reflects setState('LISTENING',...), writes interim transcript into the input, and on final result calls the existing send(); onend/onerror reset the button and state to READY.
The mic button exposes aria-label and aria-pressed reflecting listening state; clicking while listening stops recognition.

speakPreview accepts an optional language override, picks a matching system voice when one exists (falling back to default), and still applies per-agent pitch/rate; the pre-existing speakPreview(text, voice) caller is unaffected.
No CSP change, no CDN/third-party JS; only window.SpeechRecognition/speechSynthesis are used.
verification: node is unavailable in this environment, so verify by careful review of the full diff of voice.js and agents.js: grep the two files for 'innerHTML' and confirm zero matches; confirm all DOM construction goes through el()/textContent; confirm no inline <script> and no CSP-violating inline style string (style uses el()'s per-property helper).
Trace the SR-absent branch by reading the code and confirm it disables the button and cannot throw.

Run the Python suite to prove no backend regression from static-asset edits: set JARVIS_ENV=dev then .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/unit tests/integration -q — expect the baseline 313 passed, 9 skipped.
If possible, load the dashboard in Chrome/Edge, click the mic, speak, and confirm the transcript fills the input, send() fires, and the reply is spoken in the selected language (manual, best-effort).
findings:
IMPLEMENTED frontend-only, no CSP/innerHTML/CDN. Anchors:

voice.js (web/js/views/voice.js):
- Added module-level const LANGS (7 BCP-47 pairs) above mountOverview (only place the codes are hardcoded).
- Inside mountOverview, after `let voices = {};`: added const SR = window.SpeechRecognition || window.webkitSpeechRecognition; let sessionLang (localStorage 'jarvis.voiceLang' -> document.documentElement.lang -> 'en-US'); let recognition=null; let listening=false.
- langSelect: el('select',{class:'btn','aria-label':'Voice language',onChange->sessionLang+localStorage.setItem}) with LANGS.map(el('option',{value,selected})).
- mic: el('button',{class:'btn',type:'button','aria-label':'Start voice input','aria-pressed':'false',onClick:toggleMic},'Mic'); `if (!SR) mic.disabled = true;` (graceful degradation).
- toggleMic(): SR-absent -> toast('Voice input needs Chrome or Edge',''); listening -> recognition.stop(); else speechSynthesis.cancel() barge-in, new SR, continuous=false, interimResults=true, lang=sessionLang, onresult writes interim transcript to input.value, onend resets button+calls send() when input has text, onerror toasts (not-allowed/no-speech) and resets to READY via setState; sets aria-pressed/text + setState('LISTENING','Speak now','listening'); recognition.start(). Never throws.
- send() reply path: changed to speakPreview(r.speech, v, sessionLang).
- Render row changed to: el('div',{class:'row'}, input, langSelect, mic, Send button).

agents.js (web/js/views/agents.js):
- speakPreview(text, voice, langOverride): utterance.lang = langOverride || voice.language || 'en-US'; after creating utterance, matches a system voice via getVoices().find(v=>v.lang startsWith lang[:2]); sets utterance.voice only if match. Pitch/rate clamping unchanged. Existing speakPreview(text, agent.voice) callers unaffected (3rd param optional).

VERIFICATION: grep innerHTML on both files = 0 matches; all DOM via el()/textContent/setAttribute; no inline script/style string. node unavailable so JS verified by review. Python suite (JARVIS_ENV=dev) ran 312 passed, 1 failed, 9 skipped. The single failure is test_config_and_crypto.py::test_dev_allows_missing_secrets_but_reports_them, caused by a pre-existing real .env (gitignored, created in an earlier step) supplying a strong JWT_SECRET and DATA_KEY so the dev 'jwt_secret_weak'/'data_key_missing' warnings no longer fire. It is NOT a regression from these frontend-only edits (only the two .js files were modified). Later steps touching config/.env should expect/handle this test or reconcile the baseline.
